title: Risk, insurers and how insurance works
summary: The words of risk, five ways to handle it, what makes a risk insurable, how reinsurance works, and who owns an insurer.
objectives: Tell risk, exposure, hazard, peril and loss apart
Name the five methods of handling risk
List the traits of an insurable risk and explain the law of large numbers
Compare types of reinsurance, insurers and distribution systems

scenes.title: Five words of risk
scenes.src: IRMI glossary: risk; exposure; hazard; peril; National Alliance glossary: loss

items.label: Risk
items.detail: Uncertainty about whether a loss will happen

items.label: Exposure
items.detail: Being subject to loss. Also a rating unit, like payroll

items.label: Hazard
items.detail: A condition that increases the chance of loss

items.label: Peril
items.detail: The cause of loss: fire, windstorm, collision

items.label: Loss
items.detail: A reduction in value; the basis of a claim

beats.text: Risk is uncertainty about whether a loss will happen.
beats.say: Risk is uncertainty about whether a loss will happen.

beats.text: Exposure is being subject to loss. It's also a rating unit, like payroll.
beats.say: Exposure is being subject to loss. It's also a rating unit, like payroll.

beats.text: A hazard is a condition that increases the chance of loss, like poor housekeeping.
beats.say: A hazard is a condition that increases the chance of loss, like poor housekeeping.

beats.text: A peril is the cause of loss: fire, windstorm, collision.
beats.say: A peril is the cause of loss: fire, windstorm, collision.

beats.text: A loss is a reduction in value, the basis of a claim.
beats.say: A loss is a reduction in value, the basis of a claim.

scenes.title: Pure vs. speculative risk
scenes.src: IRMI glossary: pure risk; speculative risk; National Alliance glossary: speculative risk

columns.name: Pure risk
points: Chance of loss or no loss
Example: a house damaged by fire

scenes.tell: Ask: could this end in a gain? If yes, it's speculative.

beats.text: Pure risk ends only in loss or no loss, with no chance of gain. It's generally insurable.
beats.say: Pure risk ends only in loss or no loss, with no chance of gain. It's generally insurable.

beats.text: Speculative risk can bring a gain or a loss, like a new business or gambling. It's generally not insurable.
beats.say: Speculative risk can bring a gain or a loss, like a new business or gambling. It's generally not insurable.

beats.text: So ask: could this end in a gain?
beats.say: So ask: could this end in a gain?

scenes.title: The cabin Up North
scenes.src: IRMI glossary: exposure; hazard; peril; loss; hook mn-mn_core-01
scenes.story: You own a cabin Up North. Oily rags are piled next to the wood stove. One night a fire breaks out and burns part of the cabin, and you file a claim.

items.label: Exposure
items.detail: Owning the cabin: you're subject to loss

items.label: Hazard
items.detail: The oily rags: they make a fire more likely

items.label: Peril
items.detail: The fire: it causes the loss

scenes.answer: The rags are the hazard. The fire is the peril. Don't swap them.

beats.text: Here's a story. You own a cabin Up North, with oily rags piled by the wood stove. One night a fire burns part of it. Name each piece.
beats.say: Here's a story. You own a cabin Up North, with oily rags piled by the wood stove. One night a fire burns part of it. Name each piece.

beats.text: Owning the cabin is your exposure. The oily rags are the hazard, because they make a fire more likely.
beats.say: Owning the cabin is your exposure. The oily rags are the hazard, because they make a fire more likely.

beats.text: The fire is the peril, the cause. The burned value you claim is the loss.
beats.say: The fire is the peril, the cause. The burned value you claim is the loss.

beats.text: Don't swap them. The condition is the hazard; the cause is the peril.
beats.say: Don't swap them. The condition is the hazard; the cause is the peril.

scenes.q: A home has frayed, outdated electrical wiring that makes a fire more likely. In insurance terms, the wiring is a:
scenes.why: A hazard is a condition that increases the chance of loss. A fire caused by the wiring would be the peril.

beats.text: Your turn. Frayed, outdated wiring makes a house fire more likely. Is the wiring a peril, a hazard, an exposure or a loss? Pick an answer.
beats.say: Your turn. Frayed, outdated wiring makes a house fire more likely. Is the wiring a peril, a hazard, an exposure or a loss? Pick an answer.

reveal.text: It's a hazard: a condition that raises the chance of loss. A fire it starts would be the peril.
reveal.say: It's a hazard: a condition that raises the chance of loss. A fire it starts would be the peril.

scenes.title: Five ways to handle risk
scenes.src: IRMI glossary: risk sharing; hold harmless agreement; avoidance; loss control; risk retention; self-insurance
scenes.hook: Handle risk like a STARR: Share it, Transfer it, Avoid it, Reduce it, or Retain it.
items: Share: a group pools losses by a set formula, like a reciprocal
Transfer: buy insurance, or shift it by contract, like a hold-harmless
Avoid: don't do the activity. Reduce: cut how often or how badly
Retain: pay losses yourself, through deductibles or self-insurance

beats.text: Five ways to handle risk. Handle risk like a STARR: Share it, Transfer it, Avoid it, Reduce it, or Retain it.
beats.say: Five ways to handle risk. Handle risk like a STARR: Share it, Transfer it, Avoid it, Reduce it, or Retain it.

beats.text: Sharing spreads losses across a group by a set formula, like a reciprocal.
beats.say: Sharing spreads losses across a group by a set formula, like a reciprocal.

beats.text: Transfer shifts the financial consequences to someone else, by buying insurance or by a contract like a hold-harmless agreement.
beats.say: Transfer shifts the financial consequences to someone else, by buying insurance or by a contract like a hold-harmless agreement.

beats.text: Avoidance skips the activity. Reduction cuts how often losses happen, like driver training, or how bad they are, like sprinklers.
beats.say: Avoidance skips the activity. Reduction cuts how often losses happen, like driver training, or how bad they are, like sprinklers.

beats.text: Retention means paying losses yourself, with deductibles or self-insurance. A deductible retains the first part of each loss and transfers the rest.
beats.say: Retention means paying losses yourself, with deductibles or self-insurance. A deductible retains the first part of each loss and transfers the rest.

scenes.q: A trucking company keeps its trucks on the road but starts a driver-training program so fewer accidents happen. Which method of handling risk is this?
scenes.why: Driver training lowers how often losses happen. The company still runs trucks, so it has not avoided the risk.

beats.text: Quick check. A trucking company keeps driving but starts driver training so fewer accidents happen. Which method is that? Pick an answer.
beats.say: Quick check. A trucking company keeps driving but starts driver training so fewer accidents happen. Which method is that? Pick an answer.

reveal.text: Reduction. Training cuts how often losses happen. It isn't avoidance, because the company still does the activity.
reveal.say: Reduction. Training cuts how often losses happen. It isn't avoidance, because the company still does the activity.

scenes.title: What makes a risk insurable
scenes.src: Rejda & McNamara, Principles of Risk Management and Insurance (13th ed.); hook mn-mn_core-03
scenes.hook: An ideally insurable risk is a CLEAN Deal: Calculable, Large numbers, Economically feasible premium, Accidental, Not catastrophic, Determinable.
items: Calculable chance of loss; a Large number of exposure units
Economically feasible premium; an Accidental, unintentional loss
Not catastrophic: a large share of units shouldn't be hit at once
Determinable and measurable loss

beats.text: The ideal insurable risk is a CLEAN Deal.
beats.say: The ideal insurable risk is a CLEAN Deal.

beats.text: Calculable chance of loss. Large number of exposure units. Economically feasible premium. Accidental, unintentional loss.
beats.say: Calculable chance of loss. Large number of exposure units. Economically feasible premium. Accidental, unintentional loss.

beats.text: Not catastrophic. Watch out: an EXCEPT question may claim the loss should be catastrophic. It shouldn't.
beats.say: Not catastrophic. Watch out: an EXCEPT question may claim the loss should be catastrophic. It shouldn't.

beats.text: Determinable and measurable loss. Textbooks word this list differently, so learn the six ideas.
beats.say: Determinable and measurable loss. Textbooks word this list differently, so learn the six ideas.

scenes.title: Law of large numbers vs. adverse selection
scenes.src: IRMI glossary: law of large numbers; adverse selection

columns.name: Law of large numbers
points: Actual losses come closer to expected losses
A bigger pool makes the data more credible
It doesn't change any one unit's chance of loss

columns.name: Adverse selection
points: Those who see a high chance of loss buy more often
Creates an imbalance in the exposure group
Underwriting exists largely to counter it

scenes.tell: Large numbers is about the size of the pool. Adverse selection is about who chooses to join it.

beats.text: The law of large numbers: the more independent exposure units, the more likely actual losses will equal expected losses.
beats.say: The law of large numbers: the more independent exposure units, the more likely actual losses will equal expected losses.

beats.text: Adverse selection is the threat: people who see a high chance of loss buy insurance far more often. Underwriting exists largely to counter it.
beats.say: Adverse selection is the threat: people who see a high chance of loss buy insurance far more often. Underwriting exists largely to counter it.

beats.text: One is the size of the pool; the other is who joins it.
beats.say: One is the size of the pool; the other is who joins it.

scenes.title: Reinsurance: insurance for insurers
scenes.src: IRMI glossary: reinsurance; ceding company; treaty; facultative; quota share; excess of loss; capacity; surplus relief
items: Treaty
Whole classes; must accept all that qualify
Facultative
Risk by risk; reinsurer may decline
Quota share (pro rata)
Same set % of premium and of losses
Excess of loss
Pays above the retention, up to a limit

beats.text: Insurers buy insurance too. A reinsurer, for a premium, covers part or all of the liability of the primary insurer, called the ceding company.
beats.say: Insurers buy insurance too. A reinsurer, for a premium, covers part or all of the liability of the primary insurer, called the ceding company.

beats.text: A treaty covers whole classes, and the reinsurer must accept every qualifying risk. Facultative goes risk by risk, and the reinsurer may decline.
beats.say: A treaty covers whole classes, and the reinsurer must accept every qualifying risk. Facultative goes risk by risk, and the reinsurer may decline.

beats.text: Quota share, a pro rata form, shares premium and losses at the same percentage. Excess of loss pays only above the ceding company's retention, up to a limit.
beats.say: Quota share, a pro rata form, shares premium and losses at the same percentage. Excess of loss pays only above the ceding company's retention, up to a limit.

beats.text: Insurers buy it for capacity, surplus relief, stable results and catastrophe protection.
beats.say: Insurers buy it for capacity, surplus relief, stable results and catastrophe protection.

scenes.q: A reinsurer receives an agreed percentage of the premium on every policy in a class and pays that same percentage of every loss. This is:
scenes.why: Quota share is a pro rata form: premium and losses are shared at the same percentage. Excess of loss pays only above a retention; facultative goes risk by risk.

beats.text: Try this. A reinsurer takes an agreed percentage of the premium on every policy in a class and pays that percentage of every loss. Which type is it? Pick an answer.
beats.say: Try this. A reinsurer takes an agreed percentage of the premium on every policy in a class and pays that percentage of every loss. Which type is it? Pick an answer.

reveal.text: Quota share, a pro rata form. Excess of loss would pay only above the retention.
reveal.say: Quota share, a pro rata form. Excess of loss would pay only above the retention.

scenes.title: Who owns the insurer?
scenes.src: IRMI glossary: stock company; mutual company; reciprocal; Lloyd's of London

columns.name: Stock company
points: Capital fund paid in by stockholders

columns.name: Mutual company
points: Every owner is an insured, every insured an owner

scenes.tell: Follow the owner. And Lloyd's is a marketplace of underwriters, not an insurer.

beats.text: Who owns the insurer? A stock company is owned by stockholders, who need not be insureds. They pay in a capital fund.
beats.say: Who owns the insurer? A stock company is owned by stockholders, who need not be insureds. They pay in a capital fund.

beats.text: A mutual is owned by its policyholders. Every owner is an insured, and every insured is an owner.
beats.say: A mutual is owned by its policyholders. Every owner is an insured, and every insured is an owner.

beats.text: A reciprocal is an unincorporated group of subscribers who pool risks, managed by an attorney-in-fact.
beats.say: A reciprocal is an unincorporated group of subscribers who pool risks, managed by an attorney-in-fact.

beats.text: And Lloyd's isn't an insurance company. It's a marketplace of independent underwriters.
beats.say: And Lloyd's isn't an insurance company. It's a marketplace of independent underwriters.

scenes.title: Ratings and distribution systems
scenes.src: A.M. Best, Guide to Best's Financial Strength Ratings (Version 121719); IRMI: independent agency; exclusive agency; direct writer

items.label: A.M. Best: A++ and A+ Superior
items.detail: A and A- Excellent. A rating is not a recommendation to buy

items.label: Independent agency system
items.detail: Sells for one or more insurers; the agent owns the expirations

items.label: Exclusive (captive) agency
items.detail: Represents only one company or group

items.label: Direct writer
items.detail: The insurer's own employed sales force

beats.text: An A.M. Best financial strength rating is an independent opinion of an insurer's ability to meet its obligations. A plus plus and A plus are Superior; A and A minus are Excellent.
beats.say: An A M Best financial strength rating is an independent opinion of an insurer's ability to meet its obligations. A plus plus and A plus are Superior; A and A minus are Excellent.

beats.text: Independent agents sell for one or more insurers and own the expirations.
beats.say: Independent agents sell for one or more insurers and own the expirations.

beats.text: A captive agent represents one company or group. A direct writer uses its own employees.
beats.say: A captive agent represents one company or group. A direct writer uses its own employees.

items: A hazard is the condition; a peril is the cause of loss
Pure risk is generally insurable; speculative can bring a gain
STARR: Share, Transfer, Avoid, Reduce, Retain
An ideally insurable risk is a CLEAN Deal: not catastrophic
Stockholders own a stock company; policyholders own a mutual

beats.text: To recap: a hazard is the condition, a peril the cause. Pure risk is generally insurable; speculative can bring a gain.
beats.say: To recap: a hazard is the condition, a peril the cause. Pure risk is generally insurable; speculative can bring a gain.

beats.text: Handle risk like a STARR. Ideally insurable risks are a CLEAN Deal. Stockholders own a stock company; policyholders own a mutual.
beats.say: Handle risk like a STARR. Ideally insurable risks are a CLEAN Deal. Stockholders own a stock company; policyholders own a mutual.
